judgement.summary:
Step 5 is NOT acceptable as it stands; four things must land first, and all four fixes are small (I applied and measured each on a throw-away rsync copy under the session scratchpad — the real tree was never modified and no test ever pointed at ~/.cache).

What is right, re-checked by me rather than taken on trust: the §3 rows and their digest-keyed predicates (semantic_interpretation.py:1291-1329), the fresh `_EffStar` snapshot passed the just-decided version instead of reading back a fabricated record (:1316-1317), `_propagate`'s enrol/pass/raise (:1332-1353), the correction fixpoint with no await between the `results[idx] != text` test and `_write` (:1386-1390), the judge session's shape and one-round budget (JudgeTask at :766-808, `max_stalled_retries = 1` at :774), the cost breakdown (`_judge`'s `finally` at :1272-1273), and the derived permissions computed once into one local that both `allowed_tools` and the hook closure read (claude_code.py:427-429, :437, :457). Suite on my copy: 3 failed / 385 passed / 13 deselected — the three known config/API-key failures, identical before and after every mutation I ran.

The four defects: (1) the prefilter's `embed` is the first ungated call into the embedding machinery from inside an Isabelle command, so it pushes 2-3 *tracing* lines per judged entity against `editor_tracing_messages` (default 1000; overflow blocks on `Future.join` and hangs a headless frontend) — the identical hazard this package already found and fixed once for the embed phase; (2) §12 #5's "once per run" is really once per gate in flight, because the guard is read before the failing await and the flag is set after it — measured, 2 gates gave 2 lines; (3) on the prefilter timeout — the dominant failure, since the 60 s bound always cuts the provider's retry ladder before it can raise anything carrying a message — the approved line renders as a dangling colon; (4) §15.10's named step-5 deliverable, the unrequested-answer rejection, is absent: I deleted the `_NOT_ENROLLED` clause and the whole suite stayed green while an agent's unrequested answer overwrote a cached entity's record and ran a judge session on it.

The eleven derivations are all sound; only derivation 7's wording understates what it discloses (a 23-line setup block on the user-visible warning channel, not "a hint"). Nothing here needs a user decision.

rulings.title: The prefilter emits ungated Isabelle tracing per judged entity, against the 1000-message cap whose overflow blocks the command
rulings.rationale: Confirmed on the code and by my own probe. semantic_interpretation.py:1246-1248 awaits `task.emb_store.emb_provider.embed(docs, role="document")` with no gate, and the module's import block (lines 11-38) never imports `_embed_tracing_gated`, so the contextvar sits at its module default False (semantic_embedding.py:38-39). I ran a stub `Embedding_Provider` subclass against a fake connection over a throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR and counted the tracing: 2 lines when both texts miss the diskcache ('embedding 2 texts', 'done, total_tokens='), 3 when the baseline hits and the fresh text misses ('1 hits, 1 misses' in between) — and 3 is the realistic prefilter shape, since the baseline document is the one the vector store already embedded. 3 lines/entity puts the cap at ~333 judged entities. The cap is real: contrib/Isabelle2025-2/src/Pure/System/isabelle_process.ML:25-58 counts tracing per exec_id against `editor_tracing_messages`, and on overflow does `Active.dialog_text ()` plus a blocking `Future.join promise`; contrib/Isabelle2025-2/etc/options:331 defaults it to 1000 and contrib/Semantic_Embedding/etc/ ships no override (only build.props and settings). Reachability: my probe confirmed a contextvar set in the parent is visible inside a `TaskGroup.create_task` child, which is exactly how `start_gate` spawns the gate (:661-666), and the same connection contextvar is what `_report` uses at :893. What settles this as a defect rather than a plan-silent judgement call is the package's own record: this exact hazard was found, verified and fixed once before in this pipeline — archive/plans/AUTO_EMBED_AFTER_INTERPRETATION_PLAN.md:51 reads '**including the embedded machinery's own tracing** (review finding, verified) ... **plus** two provider `_log` tracing lines per `embed` call ... via `Connection.current()`, which handler tasks inherit' — and the rule is restated in three live places: semantics.py:2650-2655 gating the whole-DB embed with 'at whole-DB scale those per-batch tracing lines would overflow editor_tracing_messages', semantics.py:2499, and this module's own `_report` docstring at :960-963 ('A large cone would hit that'). Step 5 reintroduces it. The suite is blind because test_semantic_change_gate.py:112-125 replaces `embed` wholesale; it is invisible on this machine because ~/.isabelle/Isabelle2025-2/etc/preferences:5 sets editor_tracing_messages = "0", a developer preference, not shipped code. One softening nuance that does not change the ruling: `_gate` reaches `_prefilter` only when `rec.baseline_interpretation is not None` (:1377-1381), so the very first pass after the gate ships takes §3 row 2 for every legacy record and emits nothing — the storm starts one run later. The finding's own fix is the right one and I verified it.
rulings.fix: Reuse the existing gate rather than inventing a policy. Add `from .semantic_embedding import _embed_tracing_gated` to the import block (semantics.py:28 already imports this private name across modules, so it is the established pattern), then in `_prefilter` set `token = _embed_tracing_gated.set(True)` immediately before the `try` at :1246 and `_embed_tracing_gated.reset(token)` in a `finally` after the `except` arm, so the timeout and error paths reset too. Per-call scope is provably safe: each gate task carries its own copied context, so concurrent gates cannot cross tokens. Two things stay outside deliberately: `_report(..., warn=True)` at :1253 goes out on the warning channel, which the flag does not touch, and `Embedding_Provider._warn` is never gated (semantic_embedding.py:35 says so explicitly), so an unconfigured or erroring backend still reaches the user through the HTTP-error detail lines. I applied exactly this to my copy: the full suite stayed at 3 failed / 386 passed, and a probe that records `_embed_tracing_gated.get()` inside a fake provider saw True during the prefilter and False after the run. Pin it with the precedent already in this suite — archive/tests/test_complete_vector_store.py:291-299 (`_gate_recording_store`) records the flag inside the fake — by adding the same one line to `_FakeProvider.embed` (test_semantic_change_gate.py:125) and asserting it is True. The whole-run alternative (setting the token in `InterpretationTask.__enter__`/`__exit__`, currently no-op stubs at :455-459) would cover any embed added inside a run later, but it is safe only because each `interpret_file` is its own RPC handler task — an invariant the local fix does not need, so prefer the local one.

rulings.title: §12 #5 is printed once per gate in flight, not once per run
rulings.rationale: Confirmed, and I reproduced it. The ordering at semantic_interpretation.py:1249-1253 ('flag first, then report') suppresses the line only for gates that ENTER `_prefilter` after the flip; every gate already parked in the `await ... embed(...)` at :1248 passed the guard at :1242 while the flag was still False, so each runs the whole handler and each awaits `_report` at :1253. The concurrency is real: `on_answer` (:672-684) sets `_GATING` and calls `start_gate`, which does `task_group.create_task(_gate(...))` (:655-670), one `answer` call carries many entries (:865-885) and a batch is up to `_BATCH_SIZE = 20` (:145), and `_gate` runs from the `rec_cache` read straight into `await _prefilter(...)` with no lock and no other await. My probe, using the shipped `cache` fixture, `_Run`, `_FakeProvider` and `_answer_batch` with the single change of `delay > 0` (an `embed` that actually yields, as any real one does): DELAY=0.0 → 1 embed call, 1 report line; DELAY=0.01 → 2 embed calls, 2 report lines, two full tracebacks. In production the duplication is not a corner case but the norm: `_embed_cached`'s ladder (semantic_embedding.py:351-370) swallows every backend error and sleeps `2 ** attempt`, whose cumulative sleep passes 60 s during attempt 5, so `asyncio.timeout(_PREFILTER_TIMEOUT_S)` fires first and every gate of the wave sits in that 60 s window together. This is not a settled decision being re-opened: the code matches §15.5 (plan:1150-1156) literally, but that same sentence, §5.4 Failures (plan:347-350) and §12 #5 (plan:776-777) all state the goal as 'once per run', and the docstring at :1239-1241 repeats it — so the prescribed mechanism fails its own stated promise. The precedent the finding cites is exact (claude_code.py:53-57 keeps `_UNEXPECTED_BILLING_WARNED` process-wide because 'an instance-scoped flag would repeat the same line thousands of times in one collection run -- which is how a sentinel becomes wallpaper'). One clause of the finding does not stand and should be dropped, as the rebuttal says: the magnitude is NOT multiplied by concurrent theories, because `current_run_state()` (:358-363) deliberately hands out a fresh `RunState` per call until §13 step 7's lock lands and `interpret_file` resolves it once at :1600 — the scope is already per theory by design (§15.8: 'steps 3-6 run entirely on the off-lock scope'). The real bound is up to 20 duplicate lines per theory. Nothing is mis-decided (D2 still routes all of them to the judge) and no store state is harmed, but an approved user-visible line is printed N times, and the shipped test asserts a property it cannot see.
rulings.fix:
Take the rebuttal's corrected form, not the finding's inline one. Add to `RunState` (:346-355):

    def claim_prefilter_disable(self) -> bool:
        """Disable the prefilter for the rest of the run, and say whether THIS
        caller disabled it -- so §12 #5 is announced once even by the gates
        already inside the failing call when the service went down."""
        first, self.prefilter_disabled = not self.prefilter_disabled, True

and rewrite the handler at :1249-1254 as: log the traceback UNCONDITIONALLY (the host log is this module's complete record — `_report`'s docstring at :959 says 'keep logging too, so the log stays complete' — and it is the Isabelle-visible line, not the log line, that becomes wallpaper), then `if task.run_state.claim_prefilter_disable(): await _report(...)`. A method rather than an inline `first = not ...` because the read-and-flip must stay one synchronous step, and a method makes that impossible to get wrong instead of asking the next editor to remember it. Rewrite the docstring at :1239-1241: the two facts are now one because the flip and the announcement are one operation, not because of an ordering. Amend plan §15.5 (line 1150-1156) and §5.4 Failures (line 347-350) BY HAND (the project forbids scripted edits to plan documents) to say 'the caller that flips the flag is the one that reports'; §12 #5's approved text and its 'once per run' frequency are unchanged — the fix restores them. Test: parametrise `test_an_embedding_failure_skips_the_prefilter_for_the_rest_of_the_run` (test_semantic_change_gate.py:588-602) over `delay in (0.0, 0.01)` with BOTH sims raising, assert one line in both, and replace `len(provider.calls) == 1` (true only for a non-yielding fake) with `len(provider.calls) == (1 if delay == 0 else 2)`, keeping the 'no call after the flag is set' property pinned by a third entity answered in a later batch. I applied exactly this to my copy: 3 seeds all failing gave reports=1 at both delays with all 3 tracebacks retained, `prefilter_disabled` True, all three judged, versions [1,1,1], and the full suite stayed at 3 failed / 386 passed.

rulings.title: The answer tool's `_NOT_ENROLLED` refusal — a named §15.10 step-5 deliverable — is untested; removing it leaves the whole suite green
rulings.rationale: Confirmed by my own mutation on my own copy, not by trusting the finding's. Baseline: 3 failed / 385 passed / 13 deselected. Replacing `if idx is None or task.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED:` (semantic_interpretation.py:873) with `if idx is None:`: 3 failed / 385 passed / 13 deselected, byte-identical failure list. The clause is dead as far as the suite is concerned. The only nearby test, test_interpretation_driver.py:238, answers `'T.nobody'`, which is absent from `_label_to_idx` and so exercises only the `idx is None` half; `_make_task` (test_interpretation_driver.py:76-83) enrols every entry, so the state clause can never fire there; and `_answer_batch` (test_semantic_change_gate.py:288-305) builds its items from `task.unanswered_in_batch()`, so no test in the new file can answer a non-enrolled entry either. The plan names the missing test: §15.10's step-5 bullet (plan:1512-1516) reads 'unrequested-answer rejection and its mirror', and its three assertions — 'record byte-identical, no judge driver constructed, counter untouched' — cannot belong to the mirror, which needs a CHANGED verdict and therefore does construct a judge (the shipped mirror at test_semantic_change_gate.py:365-385 runs `_chain(run, {"T.a": False, "T.b": True})`, two judge sessions). They match §15.8's addressing rule instead (plan:1388-1391). This is not a re-raised step-4 ruling: the step-4 judge accepted the deferral precisely because '§15.10 schedules that coverage for the step-5 file on purpose', and step 5 is the step that did not pay it. The damage the guard prevents is concrete, and I measured it with the guard removed over a two-entry theory (`d` cached and fresh, `a` uncached) whose driver answers `T.d` with 'unrequested': `res.interpretations == ['unrequested', 'new a']`, `_rec('d').interpretation == 'unrequested'`, the raw record changed, and a judge session ran for `T.d` (`run.judged == ['T.d']`) — the agent can see a cached neighbour's name through `hover`/`desugar`/the .thy file, and only this clause stops a volunteered translation from silently overwriting and re-judging an entity the run never asked about. Severity major reflects that a deliverable the plan names for THIS step, already deferred once, is absent and guards a silent destructive branch — not a live defect: the shipped guard itself is correct step-4 code, byte-identical to `git show 5a3c201:...` line 750 and untouched by working_tree.diff.
rulings.fix:
Add the test to archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py beside the mirror. The seed must be an UNCACHED entry with a digest (§3 row 1 in `_write`, :1302-1304: `w.counter_value()`, no mint, no prefilter, no judge), so that any judge session or counter bump the run shows can only be the unrequested answer's — `_chain`'s world always constructs a judge and cannot pin those assertions. Put the unrequested entity FIRST in wire order, keeping the step-4 review's requirement that a not-enrolled entry is not the last one. I wrote and ran exactly this on my copy — it FAILS with the guard removed (`assert "Unknown entry: 'constant T.d'" in 'Batch complete. ...'`) and PASSES on the shipped code (31 passed for the module):

    def test_an_answer_for_an_entity_this_run_did_not_ask_for_is_refused(run):
        _store("d", "the d", DG["d"])                   # cached and fresh: no seed
        entries = [_entry("d", DG["d"]), _entry("a", DG["a"])]   # a uncached: the only seed
        assert _dry(entries) == 1
        before, c0 = _raw("d"), _counter()
        replies: list[str] = []

        async def act(driver, prompt):

            ret = await mk_answer_tool(driver.task).handler({"interpretations": [

        assert res.interpretations == ["the d", "new a"]
        assert run.task.state == [_NOT_ENROLLED, _DONE]
        assert _raw("d") == before, "the unrequested entity's record is byte-identical"

Docstring it against §15.8's addressing rule and name the mirror. `_NO_COST` is reachable as `SI._NO_COST` (:330); every other helper (`_store`, `_entry`, `_raw`, `_counter`, `_dry`, `run`, `accumulate_usage`, `mk_answer_tool`) is already imported or defined in the module.

rulings.title: On the prefilter timeout — the dominant failure — §12 #5's `<error>` slot renders empty
rulings.rationale: Confirmed. semantic_interpretation.py:1253 renders `{exc}`; `asyncio.timeout` raises a bare `TimeoutError`, and I measured `str(TimeoutError()) == ''`, so the user-visible line is 'The embedding service did not respond: ' — a dangling colon where §12 #5's approved template has an `<error>` slot. The slot's content is the exception's own text, not approved wording, so filling it non-emptily is a defect fix and needs no re-approval. What makes this more than an exotic path is the interaction the rebuttal established and I re-derived: `Embedding_Provider.embed` always routes through `_embed_cached`, whose `for attempt in range(10)` (semantic_embedding.py:351) swallows every backend exception and sleeps `2 ** attempt` (:368), raising the message-bearing `RuntimeError` (:370) only after the whole ladder; cumulative sleep is 1+2+4+8+16 = 31 s through attempt 4 and 63 s through attempt 5, so with `_PREFILTER_TIMEOUT_S = 60` (:181) the ladder is ALWAYS cut first. Auth rejected, network down, HTTP 500, hung socket — all arrive at :1249 as a bare `TimeoutError`. The only exceptions carrying a message are ones raised outside the ladder, which is precisely what the single exact-line test simulates (test_semantic_change_gate.py:591-605, a `ConnectionError` from the fake) — the unrepresentative case. `test_a_slow_embedding_call_is_cut_at_the_prefilter_timeout` (:608-614) asserts only the flag, the judge and the version, never the line. Severity stays minor: `_log.warning(..., exc_info=True)` at :1251-1252 keeps the full traceback in the host log, so only the user-facing half of the diagnosis is lost.
rulings.fix:
Do NOT apply the finding's own fix — I measured both variants and both are wrong. `{exc or type(exc).__name__}` is a NO-OP: `BaseException` defines neither `__bool__` nor `__len__`, so an exception is always truthy and the expression evaluates to `exc`, formatting as '' again (measured: `f'{TimeoutError() or type(...).__name__}'` → `''`). `f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"` still yields the dangling `'TimeoutError: '` in exactly the case at issue, and it would break the existing exact-line assertion at test_semantic_change_gate.py:605. Use instead, at :1253 (one expression, message-bearing case byte-identical so :605 keeps passing):

    await _report(f"The embedding service did not respond: {str(exc) or type(exc).__name__}", warn=True)

I applied this on my copy: the timeout line becomes 'The embedding service did not respond: TimeoutError', the `ConnectionError` line is unchanged, and the full suite stays at 3 failed / 386 passed. Then wrap `run.go` in `test_a_slow_embedding_call_is_cut_at_the_prefilter_timeout` (:608) in the neighbouring `_caplog_at(logging.WARNING)` helper (defined at :572) and assert that exact line, the same shape as :604-605 — today the mutation 'drop the empty-string guard' fails no test. If the implementer prefers the friendlier reading 'no answer within 60s' over the class name, note that THAT is new user-visible wording and must be proposed to the user first; the minimal form above removes the defect without needing approval.

rulings.title: An unconfigured embedding service prints the whole 23-line setup message once per seeded theory (derivation 7 understates it)
rulings.rationale: Every mechanical claim is true and I verified it, but the code change the finding asks for is rejected; what survives is a wording correction plus a commit note. Verified: `_missing_api_key_message()` (semantics.py:2740-2757) is 23 lines / 835 chars, `_resolve_embedding_config` pushes it to `connection.warning` BEFORE raising (semantics.py:2795-2802), and `_conn_semantic_vector_store` calls that resolution at semantics.py:2827 BEFORE the registry read at :2830-2833, so a raise memoises nothing and every theory repeats it; step 5 really is the first per-theory resolution inside the run (`git show 5a3c201:...semantic_interpretation.py | grep semantic_vector_store` returns nothing, and the new call is at :1720 inside `if seeds:`). But there is no plan/code disagreement, which is the bar this review sets: §15.8 (plan:1408-1415) prescribes verbatim what is on disk — 'skipped when `run_state.prefilter_disabled` is already set, and otherwise inside `except Exception` ⇒ `emb_store = None` with a host-log line only' — and assigns the remedy elsewhere, while §5.6 (plan:485-486) states it flatly ('`semantic_vector_store` threads `warn` through so the per-theory resolution of §15.8 never repeats it') and §13 puts §5.6 in step 6. semantic_interpretation.py:1717-1723 is exactly that. Derivation 7 gets the mechanism and the step-6 ownership right; what it understates is only the size, calling a 23-line block on the user-visible warning channel 'a hint'. Severity is further diluted by pre-existing behaviour the finding does not mention: `_query_knn` resolves the store on every retrieval (semantics.py:2942), so repeated emission already happens outside this pipeline for an unconfigured user.
rulings.fix: Change no code — semantic_interpretation.py:1717-1723 stays exactly as it is. Two things NOT to do, both of which I checked: do not pull step 6's `warn=False` hop forward, because §12 #4 is printed by the step-6 startup check (§5.6, D16) and threading `warn` without it would leave an unconfigured user with no user-visible explanation at all during the whole interpretation phase, only the host-log line at :1722; and do not set `run_state.prefilter_disabled` in that except branch, because `current_run_state()` (:358-363) hands out a fresh `RunState` per `interpret_file` until §13 step 7, so the flag cannot cross a theory boundary and the write would be inert. What is owed is two lines of bookkeeping: (1) sharpen derivation 7 from 'prints `_resolve_embedding_config`'s hint per theory' to 'prints the whole 23-line `_missing_api_key_message` on the user-visible warning channel, once per seeded theory (semantics.py:2795-2802; nothing is memoised, because the resolution at 2827 precedes the registry read at 2830)'; (2) put the same sentence in the step-5 commit message with 'until §13 step 6 threads D16's `warn` through `semantic_vector_store`', so nobody runs step 5 against a real cone unconfigured and files it as a regression. Worth carrying into the step-6 review, not acting on here: after step 6 lands, the startup check's `prefilter_disabled` still will not reach `interpret_file` until step 7 gives `current_run_state()` something to return, so `warn=False` — not the flag — must be what actually silences the repetition in that window.

findings.title: §12 #5 is printed once per gate in flight, not once per run: the "printed once" guarantee does not survive concurrency
findings.location: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:1242 (the guard) and :1249-1254 (the handler); the claim in the docstring at :1239-1241 and in plan §5.4 "Failures" / §12 #5
findings.claim: The prefilter's failure policy promises one user-visible line per run (§12 #5 "once per run"; §5.4 "the flag set before the report so 'skipped for the rest of the run' and 'printed once' are one fact"; the docstring at :1239-1241 repeats the claim). The ordering "flag first, then report" only suppresses the line for gates that ENTER `_prefilter` after the first failure. Gates that are already parked in the `await ... embed(...)` at :1248 passed the `prefilter_disabled` guard at :1242 while the flag was still False, so each of them runs the whole handler and each awaits `_report` at :1253. With a real embedding provider (which yields on network I/O) every gate of the batch is in flight at once, so a single outage prints the line once per concurrently-gating entity -- up to `_BATCH_SIZE` = 20 per theory, multiplied by the theories `schedule_dag` runs at the same time -- each with its own full `exc_info` traceback in the host log. Nothing is mis-decided (D2 still resolves them all through the judge), but the approved user-visible text is duplicated, which is exactly the "a sentinel becomes wallpaper" failure the same package guards against elsewhere (claude_code.py:55-57, `_UNEXPECTED_BILLING_WARNED`).
findings.evidence: Measured. I ran a probe against a throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR, reusing the shipped harness of archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py: two seeds `a` and `b` whose records both carry a digest and a baseline, answered in one `answer` call, with `_FakeProvider(sims={"new a": ConnectionError(...), "new b": ConnectionError(...)}, delay=0.01)` -- the only change from the shipped test being `delay > 0`, i.e. an `embed` that actually yields to the loop, as a real provider does. Result: `len(provider.calls) == 2` and two report lines, `['The embedding service did not respond: embedding service down', 'The embedding service did not respond: embedding service down']`, plus two `prefilter: the embedding call failed` warnings with tracebacks (semantic_interpretation.py:1251 twice, :965 twice). The shipped test `test_an_embedding_failure_skips_the_prefilter_for_the_rest_of_the_run` (archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py:588-602) asserts `lines == [...one line...]`, but it passes only because `_FakeProvider.embed` with `delay == 0` contains no `await` that yields, so gate `a` runs its whole `_prefilter` -- guard, embed, except-handler, flag -- without ever giving gate `b` a turn. The test therefore does not pin the property it names.
findings.fix: Make the report conditional on being the caller that flipped the flag, not on the flag's value at entry -- the flip is synchronous, so exactly one handler can win: in the `except` block at :1249, capture `first = not task.run_state.prefilter_disabled` BEFORE setting it, then `task.run_state.prefilter_disabled = True`, and guard `await _report(...)` (and, if wanted, the `exc_info=True` log) with `if first:`. Then extend the shipped test with `delay > 0` on both entries so the regression is pinned; today's `delay == 0` variant cannot see it.

findings.title: The prefilter emits Isabelle *tracing* lines per judged entity — the one channel this pipeline forbids at cone scale
findings.claim: `_prefilter` calls `Embedding_Provider.embed` without setting the `_embed_tracing_gated` contextvar, so every judged entity pushes 2-3 `Connection.tracing` messages into the Isabelle command that is running the interpretation. Every other bulk embed site in this package gates that tracing precisely because it overflows `editor_tracing_messages`; exceeding the cap (default 1000) pops Isabelle's own blocking "Tracing paused" dialog, and hangs a headless frontend outright. A run that judges more than roughly 330-500 entities under one `by aoa` / `run_semantic_interpretation` command therefore wedges the very command it is reporting on.
findings.evidence:
`Embedding_Provider._log` (semantic_embedding.py:433-439) returns early only `if _embed_tracing_gated.get()`, otherwise `await conn.tracing(msg)` on `Connection.current()`. `embed` (:456-468) calls it twice per call — `"[Embedding] <model>: embedding 2 texts, N chars"` (:465) and `"[Embedding] <model>: done, total_tokens=..."` (:467) — and `_embed_cached` adds a third when the diskcache has any hit (:337 "all N texts cached" / :340 "H hits, M misses"). `_prefilter` sets no gate, so all of these fire.

The gate is the established mechanism: `_embed_all` (semantics.py:2655) does `token = _embed_tracing_gated.set(not verbose)` with the comment at :2650-2652 "at whole-DB scale those per-batch tracing lines would overflow editor_tracing_messages". And this module's own `_report` docstring (semantic_interpretation.py:960-963) states the rule for exactly this pipeline: "writeln, not tracing: tracing is capped by the `editor_tracing_messages` option (default 1000) and exceeding it pops Isabelle's own blocking 'Tracing paused' dialog (isabelle_process.ML:35-60). A large cone would hit that."

The connection is reachable from the gate: `_connection_var` is a `contextvars.ContextVar` (contrib/Isabelle_RPC/Isabelle_RPC_Host/rpc.py:19), the gate tasks are created by `task_group.create_task` from inside the answer-tool handler (whose own `await _report(...)` at semantic_interpretation.py:893 depends on the same contextvar), and `create_task` copies that context — so `Connection.current()` is set inside `_prefilter` and the tracing really is sent. 1) Is the concurrency real, or do gates serialise? Real. `InterpretationTask.on_answer` (semantic_interpretation.py:672-684) calls `start_gate`, which does `self.task_group.create_task(_gate(self, idx))` (:655-670) — every answered entry gets its own task in `interpret_file`'s group. Serialisation would need the fake's property of never yielding — see (2).

2) Would a real provider yield before failing? Yes, unavoidably. `Semantic_Embedder.embed` (semantic_embedding.py:455-469) awaits `self._log(f"[Embedding] {self.model}: embedding ...")` BEFORE `self._embed_cached(...)`, and `_log` goes out over the connection. So even a failure that is local to the process (bad config, cache error) is preceded by an await that yields, and every gate already in flight has passed the `prefilter_disabled` guard at :1242 while the flag was still False. Each then runs the full handler at :1249-1254: sets the flag (already True), logs a full traceback, and awaits `_report(...)`.

3) Is it settled by the plan, i.e. is the code merely doing what was approved? The code matches §15.5 literally ("set `task.run_state.prefilter_disabled = True` FIRST, then log and `await _report(...)`" — plan:1150-1156), but the plan's stated GOAL in the very same sentence, and in §5.4 Failures (plan:347-350) and §12 #5 (plan:776-777), is "once per run". The prescribed ordering achieves that only against gates that ENTER `_prefilter` after the flip; it cannot suppress the ones already parked in the await. Nothing is mis-decided (D2 still routes all of them to the judge), no store state is harmed, and my fix-probe confirmed the writes are identical with and without the fix. Every mechanical claim is true — I reproduced it — but as a step-5 *defect* it does not stand: the code matches the plan word for word, and what actually survives is a wording correction to derivation 7 plus a commit note.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (probe + code)

1. The message really is the full setup block, not a line. A probe against the module on disk (env stripped of EMBEDDING_API_KEY/FIREWORKS_API_KEY/EMBEDDING_BASE_URL/DRIVER/MODEL, SEMANTIC_DB_DIR pointed at a throw-away dir, a fake connection recording `warning`) printed: `LINES: 23 CHARS: 835`. 2. It really repeats, and nothing is memoised. The same probe called `_conn_semantic_vector_store(conn)` three times: "theory 0/1/2 raised RuntimeError", "warnings emitted: 3", "each identical to full message: True", "cache attr: ABSENT". The cause is the ordering the finding names: semantics.py:2827 `driver, base_url, model, api_key = await _resolve_embedding_config(self)` runs *before* the registry read at semantics.py:2830-2833, and the registry is only ever populated from the `Semantic_Vector_Store.__init__` at semantics.py:2012-2020, which the raise never reaches.

3. Step 5 really is the first per-theory resolution inside the interpretation run. `git show 5a3c201:Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py | grep -n "semantic_vector_store\|emb_store"` returns nothing; the new call is semantic_interpretation.py:1720 inside `if seeds:`. In the run's ML flow (Tools/interpret_command.ML:149-152) `interpret_with_parallel` runs *first* and `embed_phase ()` (semantics.py:2898, one resolution) only afterwards, so the N per-theory copies do land before the single copy the user already got at step 4.

4. The test does dodge the user-visible half: archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py:158-162 `async def semantic_vector_store(self): ... raise RuntimeError("no embedding service is configured")` — a bare raise, no `warning` call.

WHY IT IS ONLY "PARTLY"

a) There is no plan/code disagreement, which is the bar this review sets. §13 orders step 5 before step 6 ("6. `Config.lookup` callback with `cfg_context`; startup check RPC (§5.6)"), and §15.8 prescribes exactly the code that is on disk: "skipped when `run_state.prefilter_disabled` is already set, and otherwise inside `except Exception` ⇒ `emb_store = None` with a host-log line only ...; D16's `warn` is threaded one hop further through `semantic_vector_store` so the multi-line hint is not repeated per theory." semantic_interpretation.py:1717-1723 is that, verbatim. The implementer is following the plan, and the plan already owns the remedy.

b) Derivation 7 does not misstate the *mechanism* — "prints `_resolve_embedding_config`'s hint per theory" gets the per-theory multiplication and the step-6 ownership right. What is understated is only the size ("hint" for a 23-line block on the warning channel). That is a wording fix to a derivation note, not a code finding.

c) The severity is further diluted by precedent the finding does not mention: the same 23-line block is already emitted once per *retrieval* for an unconfigured user, because `_query_knn` (semantics.py:2942) resolves the store on every query. Repeated emission is pre-existing system behaviour for someone who has configured nothing; step 5 extends it to the interpretation phase.

d) The finding's primary fix is worse than doing nothing. Threading `warn=False` into step 5 without §5.6's startup check (which is what prints text §12 #4 once) would leave the unconfigured user with *no* user-visible explanation at all during the whole interpretation phase — only a host-log line at semantic_interpretation.py:1722 — until `embed_phase` fails at the end. The plan pairs the two on purpose ("the startup check passes `warn=False` and prints #4 itself, so the hint appears once (D16)", §5.6).

`_JUDGE_SESSIONS` (:184) as a module-level `asyncio.Semaphore(40)`: CPython's Semaphore binds a loop only when `acquire` has to wait, and the RPC host runs one event loop for the process (nothing in the package wraps `interpret_file` in its own `asyncio.run`), so the loop-binding hazard the test fixture guards against is a test-only artefact. Cancellation while waiting for a permit is safe -- `Semaphore.acquire` restores the value and wakes the next waiter before re-raising -- and `_judge`'s `except Exception` does not swallow it, while the `finally` still books the judge's cost. The permit wraps the session only, gates start at the answer regardless, and the loop's wake-up comes from `gate_finished`, so the cap cannot deadlock the queue (verified by test_judge_sessions_are_capped_and_each_holds_one_entity: `gates_running == 5` with 2 open sessions).
